newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia names new head of controversial sports fund.
newsitem.headline: Russia names new head of controversial sports fund.

text.p: Russia's National Sports Fund (NSF), a controversial body with huge financial resources that has been at the centre of recent Kremlin intrigue, named a new president on Thursday in a bid to clean up its image.

Itar-Tass news agency said Vladimir Vasin, deputy head of the Russian Olympic Committee, was elected at a special NSF conference to replace Sergei Leonyuk. The NSF enjoys lucrative alcohol and tobacco import privileges to raise funds for sports.

Tass said a previous NSF president, Boris Fyodorov, was also reinstated as a vice president after appealing against his removal earlier this year. Fyodorov, who promised to submit details of NSF accounts, narrowly escaped assassination in June.
The NSF conference said Russian sport was in dire need of cash to prepare for the 1998 Winter Olympics and it agreed to reinstate Fyodorov for a trial period only, Tass said.
A final decision on Fyodorov will be taken at the next conference in January, it added.
Tass said several NSF leaders called for personnel changes to reform the organisation whose image has been tainted by a series of allegations of shady financial dealings.

Tass quoted Russian Olympic Committee President Vitaly Smirnov, who chaired the conference, as saying society should be informed of the NSF's cash resources and play a role in their distribution for various programmes.
Fyodorov appeared on television earlier this month to repeat allegations of blackmail against Alexander Korzhakov, President Boris Yeltsin's former top bodyguard and long time confidant.
Korzhakov denied the accusation, first made in a newspaper article soon after the assassination attempt.
Fyodorov said two attackers stabbed him 12 times in June near his apartment bloc in a posh Moscow residential area.
Earlier in the year Fyodorov was detained for several days by police on suspicion that he was involved in drug sales.
